subject: Hosting lane arbitrage & region geofence: MAP milestones and acceptance gates
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@aurorahealth.com>, procurement@aurorahealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosting lane arbitrage & region geofence: MAP milestones and acceptance gates

Emma / Aurora team —

Thanks again for the meeting today. Attached is an updated mutual action plan (MAP_Aurora_v3.xlsx) that consolidates the timelines we sketched out and a hosting-costs snapshot (hosting_costs_v2.pdf). Two immediate asks I want to confirm so we can lock milestone owners:

1) Deployment lane preference: you mentioned a preference to start in our Hosted environment for speed to market, then evaluate Dedicated for predictable throughput, with Private kept as an acceptance option if the compliance review requires it. Please confirm that ordering (Hosted -> Dedicated pilot -> Private) is still correct.

2) Region/geofence: you flagged US-east for PHI residency. Please confirm the geofence requirement (US-east only) vs. allowance for fallbacks to other US regions in case of capacity.

If those two items are green, we will:
- Publish a POC plan for Hosted (2-week functional POC, baseline latency/cost tests)
- Spin up a 30-day Dedicated pilot (if you want to evaluate throughput under production traffic profile)
- Prepare a Private deployment estimate and a timeline for on-prem network assessment (if triggered)

Attached: MAP_Aurora_v3.xlsx (workback schedule), hosting_costs_v2.pdf (ballpark ops TCO).

Proposed next steps: confirm the two bullets above by EOD Wed 3/31, then we schedule a 30-minute technical alignment (Karthik + Priyom) for the POC acceptance criteria.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
(attachment: MAP_Aurora_v3.xlsx (xlsx), hosting_costs_v2.pdf (pdf))

From: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@aurorahealth.com>

Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting lane arbitrage & region geofence: MAP milestones and acceptance gates

Thanks Marissa — that looks good as a starting point. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- Ordering preference is correct: Hosted first, then Dedicated pilot. Private is only required if the compliance team deems the Hosted/Dedicated options insufficient for PHI.
- Data residency: requirement is US-only, with primary preference for us-east-1. We can consider another US region as a fallback but need confirmation that logs and backups remain within US boundaries.

Procurement: we will need a short summary of committed capacity (min GPUs / vCPU baseline) and a rough MRR estimate for the Dedicated pilot so we can align on budgeting. Also happy to get SOC2 evidence and the legal template for initial review.

Emma
Director, Digital Products | Aurora Health
emma.lewis@aurorahealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting lane arbitrage & region geofence: MAP milestones and acceptance gates

Echoing Marissa and Emma — quick technical sketch for the evaluation plan so we can bake acceptance gates into the MAP:

POC (Hosted) — 2 weeks- Objective: validate functional correctness + baseline latency/cost- Acceptance: 95th perc < 600ms for 1kRPS synthetic baseline; end-to-end latency trace present; prefix-cache warm-up < 50ms per request- Tests: synthetic traffic replay (1kRPS), prompt regression suite, prefix-KV warm start

Dedicated Pilot — 30 days- Objective: validate throughput, scaling, and cost under realistic traffic; run production-like traffic for a 72h soak- Acceptance: sustained 95th perc < 350ms at target throughput; autoscaling events < 2% error rate; cost delta vs Hosted within agreed band

Private (if triggered) — network assessment + 6-week bake- Objective: validate on-prem packaging, KMS/HSM integration, and audit log delivery

Attachments: eval_playbook_hosted.md (detailed tests), short checklist we can drop into the MAP.

I can run the Hosted test harness if you want — suggest we reserve a 60-min alignment Tues 3/31 with Aurora engineers to confirm SLO targets and synthetic workloads.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(attachment: eval_playbook_hosted.md (md))

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting lane arbitrage & region geofence: MAP milestones and acceptance gates

Thanks team — I updated the MAP spreadsheet with the technical milestones Karthik suggested and added an explicit canary+rollback plan for the Hosted -> Dedicated transition. Key changes:

- POC (Hosted): target kickoff 2026-04-06, completion 2026-04-20
- Dedicated pilot: target start 2026-05-01, 30-day pilot window
- Private: placeholder estimate and "trigger criteria" row (compliance sign-off required)

Canary rollback plan (summary):
- Canary window 48h, monitor key metrics (latency 95th, error rate, token-cost variance). If any metric crosses threshold for >30m, auto-failover to Hosted variant and scale back Dedicated pool by 20%.

I also attached a short canary checklist (canary-rollback-plan.txt) in the MAP folder. If procurement needs committed capacity numbers for the Dedicated pilot, I can put together a nominal baseline (we normally recommend a 4-GPU pool to start for the traffic profile you described).

-Priyom
Manager, Solutions Ops | Redwood Inference
(attachment: canary-rollback-plan.txt (txt))

From: Procurement Team <procurement@aurorahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting lane arbitrage & region geofence: MAP milestones and acceptance gates

Marissa — thanks for the updates. A couple procurement items to keep the cadence moving:

1) Please provide an estimated monthly recurring charge (MRR) for the proposed Dedicated 4-GPU pilot and a line for Hosted consumption for a 30-day window at your tested baseline.
2) We need SOC 2 Type II evidence or access to your compliance package for legal intake. If possible, share a SOC2 excerpt or a redacted report and the standard data processing addendum (DPA).
3) Contract ask: please upload a draft Master Services Agreement (MSA) or DocuSign template so our legal can start the first pass.

Target: procurement needs the items above by 2026-04-07 to stay on schedule for a May pilot.

Procurement Team
Aurora Health
(attachment requested: SOC2_request_form.pdf)

Great, good momentum — next steps and owners: 

- Marissa: deliver draft MSA (DocuSign template) + hosted consumption estimate by 2026-04-02. Link will be uploaded to the MAP drive.
- Priyom: finalize Dedicated 4-GPU pilot MRR estimate and baseline capacity numbers by 2026-04-02.
- Karthik: prep the Hosted POC harness and acceptance checklist; schedule the Tues 3/31 tech alignment (60min).
- Irene: prepare SOC2 redacted excerpt + compliance packet and share with Procurement by 2026-04-06.

Emma — once Procurement confirms the budgetary OK on 4/7 we will lock the pilot start for 5/1. If Aurora confirms that US-east restriction is firm, we'll set the Hosted POC and Dedicated pilot to use us-east resources and include geofence verification in the acceptance tests.

I'll upload the updated MAP and draft MSA to the sheet link you have (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AuroraMAP) and ping the DocuSign template link when it's ready. Meeting invite for the tech alignment will go out in ~15 minutes.

Thanks everyone —
Marissa Cole
